lessons.title: Story Time: A Tale of Two Climates
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to compare two settings in a story.
success_criteria: I can describe a hot setting.
I can describe a cold setting.
lessons.starter_activity: Sort pictures into hot and cold places.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Read a story featuring both a hot and cold setting, modelling comparison.
lessons.independent_task: Children compare the two settings, recording one feature of each.
key_questions: What is the hot setting like?
What is the cold setting like?

differentiation.greater_depth: Compare in full sentences with reasoning

lessons.assessment_notes: Note comprehension of contrasting settings — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.home_link: Describe a hot and cold place you know.

lessons.title: Comparing Temperature Recap
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to compare and order temperatures using a hot/cold places context.
success_criteria: I can say which place is hotter.
I can order 3 places by temperature.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model ordering places by temperature using picture/data cards.
lessons.independent_task: Children order hot/cold place cards by temperature.
key_questions: Which place is hottest?
Can you order these three?
lessons.assessment_notes: Record temperature comparison consolidation — evidence for MATHS.MEA.
lessons.home_link: Compare temperatures of places you know.

lessons.title: Where Are the Hottest and Coldest Places?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to locate hot and cold regions on a world map.
success_criteria: I can find a hot region on a map.
I can find a cold region on a map.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Introduce the equator and poles simply, linking to hot and cold regions.
lessons.independent_task: Children mark hot regions (near the equator) and cold regions (near the poles) on a world map.
key_questions: Where is it hottest?
Where is it coldest?

differentiation.greater_depth: Explain why the equator is hot and poles are cold simply

lessons.assessment_notes: Note locational knowledge of climate zones — evidence for GEOG.2.
lessons.home_link: Find the equator or poles on a globe if available.

lessons.title: Animals of Hot Places
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe how an animal is suited to a hot climate.
success_criteria: I can name an animal from a hot place.
I can say one way it copes with heat.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at pictures of desert animals.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss how animals like camels are adapted to survive in hot places.
lessons.independent_task: Children draw a hot-place animal and label an adaptation.
key_questions: How does this animal cope with heat?
What helps it survive?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note early adaptation understanding — evidence for SCI.ANI.
lessons.home_link: Look up a desert animal together.

lessons.title: Writing About a Hot or Cold Place
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to write descriptive sentences about a hot or cold place.
success_criteria: I can describe a hot or cold place.
I can write a full sentence.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model writing a descriptive sentence about a hot or cold place using adjectives.
lessons.independent_task: Children write 2-3 descriptive sentences about a chosen hot or cold place.
key_questions: What does this place look/feel like?
Can you write a sentence about it?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note descriptive vocabulary and sentence construction — evidence for ENG.W2/W3.
lessons.home_link: Describe a hot or cold place to your family.

lessons.title: Word Problems: Packing for a Trip
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to solve addition/subtraction word problems using a travel context.
success_criteria: I can solve an addition problem.
I can solve a subtraction problem.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model solving word problems about packing items for a hot or cold trip.
lessons.independent_task: Children solve travel-themed word problems, showing working.
key_questions: How many items altogether?
How many are left?
lessons.assessment_notes: Record word problem solving skill — evidence for MATHS.N2.
lessons.home_link: Make up a packing word problem for your family.

lessons.title: What Would You Pack? Hot vs Cold Trip
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to select suitable items for a hot or cold place.
success_criteria: I can choose an item for a hot trip.
I can choose an item for a cold trip.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap hot and cold place features.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss what you would need to pack differently for a hot vs cold destination.
lessons.independent_task: Children sort packing item picture cards into 'hot trip' and 'cold trip', explaining reasoning.
key_questions: Why would you pack this for a hot place?
Why not for a cold place?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note application of climate knowledge to a practical context — evidence for GEOG.2.
lessons.home_link: Help pack for a real or pretend trip at home.

lessons.title: Animals of Cold Places
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe how an animal is suited to a cold climate.
success_criteria: I can name an animal from a cold place.
I can say one way it copes with cold.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at pictures of polar animals.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss how animals like polar bears are adapted to survive in cold places (thick fur, blubber).
lessons.independent_task: Children draw a cold-place animal and label an adaptation.
key_questions: How does this animal cope with cold?
What helps it survive?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note adaptation understanding, comparing hot/cold — evidence for SCI.ANI.
lessons.home_link: Look up a polar animal together.

lessons.title: Phonics: Reading Climate Words
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to blend and read hot/cold-themed words.
success_criteria: I can blend and read climate words.
I can read a sentence about hot or cold places.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Introduce/reinforce a grapheme, blending hot/cold-themed words (e.g. 'sun', 'ice', 'heat').
lessons.independent_task: Children read themed word and sentence cards.
key_questions: Can you blend this word?
Can you read this sentence?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note phonics application — evidence for ENG.R1.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate reading progress with a themed reading game.
lessons.home_link: Practise reading climate words over the week.

lessons.title: Place Value Recap: Numbers to 30
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to represent numbers to 30 using tens and ones.
success_criteria: I can show a number using tens and ones.
I can say how many tens and ones make a number to 30.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap tens and ones from Week 5/20.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model representing numbers up to 30 using base-10 blocks.
lessons.independent_task: Children represent given numbers to 30 using tens and ones blocks.
key_questions: How many tens and ones make this number?
Can you show me 27?
lessons.assessment_notes: Record extended place value understanding — evidence for MATHS.N1.
lessons.home_link: Practise representing numbers with grouped objects.

lessons.title: How Do People Live in Hot Places?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe how people adapt their lives to a hot climate.
success_criteria: I can name one way people cope with heat.
I can say why it helps.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss how people keep cool in hot weather.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss how people in hot climates adapt (light clothing, shade, siesta, housing design).
lessons.independent_task: Children record one way people adapt to hot climates, with a simple explanation.
key_questions: How do people stay cool in hot places?
Why does this help?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note understanding of human adaptation to climate — evidence for GEOG.2.
lessons.plenary: Recap ways people cope with heat.
lessons.home_link: Talk about how your family copes with hot weather.

lessons.title: Hot or Cold? Class Debate
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to state and justify a preference between hot and cold places.
success_criteria: I can say my preference.
I can give one reason for it.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model stating an opinion with a reason: 'I would prefer a hot place because...'
lessons.independent_task: Children state and justify their preference in a class discussion, listening respectfully to others.
key_questions: Would you prefer a hot or cold place? Why?
Can you listen to a different opinion?

differentiation.greater_depth: Respond respectfully to a differing opinion

lessons.assessment_notes: Note ability to state and justify an opinion — evidence for ENG.SL1.
lessons.plenary: Recap the range of opinions shared.
lessons.home_link: Discuss with your family whether they'd prefer hot or cold places.

lessons.title: Data Handling: Class Hot/Cold Survey
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to record and interpret data from a class survey.
success_criteria: I can record a survey using tally marks.
I can say which was more popular.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model conducting a class survey on hot vs cold preference, recording with tally marks.
lessons.independent_task: Children help conduct and record the survey, then answer simple questions about the results.
key_questions: Which was more popular?
How many more chose hot places?
lessons.assessment_notes: Record data handling consolidation — evidence for MATHS.MEA.
lessons.home_link: Do a simple survey with your family.

lessons.title: How Do People Live in Cold Places?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe how people adapt their lives to a cold climate.
success_criteria: I can name one way people cope with cold.
I can say why it helps.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss how people keep warm in cold weather.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss how people in cold climates adapt (layered clothing, insulated housing, warm food).
lessons.independent_task: Children record one way people adapt to cold climates, with a simple explanation.
key_questions: How do people stay warm in cold places?
Why does this help?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note understanding of human adaptation to climate, comparing to hot places — evidence for GEOG.2.
lessons.plenary: Recap ways people cope with cold.
lessons.home_link: Talk about how your family copes with cold weather.

lessons.title: Hot and Cold Places Quiz
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to answer comprehension questions about hot and cold places.
success_criteria: I can answer a retrieval question.
I can answer an inference question.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Read a summary passage about hot and cold places, modelling retrieval and inference questions.
lessons.independent_task: Children answer a mix of retrieval and inference questions about the passage.
key_questions: Where is it hottest on Earth?
Why do polar animals have thick fur?

differentiation.support: Answer retrieval questions with text pointing

lessons.assessment_notes: Note comprehension progress — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.home_link: Quiz your family on hot and cold place facts.

lessons.title: Maths Review: Place Value and Data
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to apply place value and data handling skills learned this week.
success_criteria: I can represent numbers with tens and ones.
I can read a tally chart.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Quick recap of place value and data handling.
lessons.independent_task: Children rotate through 2 stations: place value, data handling.
key_questions: How many tens and ones?
What does the tally show?
lessons.assessment_notes: Summarise week 29 maths observations for each child — evidence for MATHS.N1/MEA.
lessons.plenary: Class recap game combining both skills.
lessons.home_link: Continue practising place value over the weekend.

lessons.title: Hot and Cold Places Topic Recap
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to summarise key learning about hot and cold places and animal adaptation.
success_criteria: I can name a hot-place and a cold-place animal.
I can describe an adaptation for each.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the week's science and geography vocabulary.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Quick recap quiz format covering hot/cold regions, animal adaptations, and human adaptations.
lessons.independent_task: Children complete a review worksheet and contribute to a class 'Hot and Cold Places' display.
key_questions: What have we learned about hot and cold places?
What was most interesting?

differentiation.support: Word bank and picture support provided

lessons.assessment_notes: Note climate/adaptation understanding progress — evidence for SCI.ANI/GEOG.2.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate the week's hot and cold places learning.
lessons.home_link: Share what you learned with your family.
